module

public import FormalConjecturesForMathlib.LinearAlgebra.GeneralLinearGroup

@[expose] public section

open Matrix
open scoped MatrixGroups

variable (n : Type*) [DecidableEq n] [Fintype n] (R : Type*) [CommRing R]

/-- The group of invertible diagonal matrices with determinant 1. -/
def Matrix.SpecialLinearGroup.diagonalSubgroup : Subgroup (SpecialLinearGroup n R) :=
  (Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.diagonalSubgroup n R).comap Matrix.SpecialLinearGroup.toGL

findings.description: In FormalConjectures/Arxiv/2504.17644/Margulis.lean:93–96, the quotient uses the range of `SpecialLinearGroup.map (polyToLaurent F)`. However, `polyToLaurent` (lines 70–71) sends `Polynomial.X` to `HahnSeries.single 1 1`, and Mathlib gives `F⸨X⸩` the X-adic topology. To represent the source's F((t⁻¹)), the series variable X must represent t⁻¹, so the polynomial variable t must instead map to `HahnSeries.single (-1) 1`. This is not a harmless renaming: the current Γ is contained in the compact-open subgroup U = SL₄(F[[X]]), rather than being the source's infinity-place lattice. Indeed, no D-orbit in the current quotient can have compact closure: its continuous image in the discrete space G/U is infinite, since otherwise the non-relatively-compact group D would be contained in finitely many compact translates of U. Lean experiments verified both generator images, their opposite valuation inequalities, and that every entry of the current Γ has valuation ≤ 1. The reusable `diagonalSubgroup` definition itself is correct.
findings.source_evidence: Huang–Shi, “Bounded diagonal orbits in homogeneous spaces over function fields,” arXiv:2504.17644v3, Introduction immediately before Theorem 1.2, defines K = F((t⁻¹)), embeds F[t] into K, and specifies |btˡ| = pˡ for nonzero b. Theorem 1.2 asserts a non-closed relatively compact D-orbit in SL₄(K)/SL₄(F[t]) for characteristic 3, 5, 7, or 11. Read in bounded_orbits.tex, lines 228–242, from https://arxiv.org/e-print/2504.17644v3; abstract page: https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.17644v3. Mathlib's LaurentSeries.valued and valuation_single_zpow confirm the X-adic convention used by Lean.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the body of `Margulis.polyToLaurent` with `Polynomial.eval₂RingHom (algebraMap F F⸨X⸩) (HahnSeries.single (-1 : ℤ) (1 : F))`, interpreting the Laurent-series variable as t⁻¹. Keep the induced special-linear-group map in the quotient. This replacement was checked in the scratch file. No change to `Matrix.SpecialLinearGroup.diagonalSubgroup` is needed.

reformulations.difference: The subgroup is constructed as the preimage, along SL → GL, of the image of tuples of units, rather than directly imposing zero off-diagonal entries or specifying diagonal entries with product one.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The map `toGL` preserves the underlying matrix. The GL diagonal homomorphism sends a tuple of units to its diagonal matrix, and `Matrix.isUnit_diagonal` ensures that every invertible diagonal matrix arises this way. Consequently, for every `g : SpecialLinearGroup n R`, membership is equivalent to `(g : Matrix n n R).IsDiag`, and also to the existence of `d : n → R` with `∏ i, d i = 1` and `↑g = Matrix.diagonal d`. Both equivalences were proved in /workspace/review/scratch.lean for arbitrary finite n and commutative R, without nonemptiness or nontriviality assumptions.

review.notes: The sole declaration in the reviewed library file is mathematically faithful; the finding is an independent defect discovered in its function-field use site. The real use site, Margulis.conjecture_1_1, agrees with the cited Conjecture 1.1. No duplicate diagonal-subgroup declaration was found in Mathlib. Both scratch.lean and embedding.lean compile successfully, and their checked lemmas have no sorry dependencies. Boundary tests covered empty and singleton dimensions, the zero ring, ZMod 0, finite fields, and rings with zero divisors (ZMod 4 and ZMod 6).
